context: Evaluates implementation of a stack-based navigation Pinia store that derives dual-panel state from a stack of NavLevel objects. Key aspects tested are the leftPanel/rightPanel computed logic, the distinction between push navigation (openNotebook) and replace navigation (openNotebookFromLeft), and the collapse-to-root behaviour of selectNoteFromRoot.

checklist.name: NavLevel / NavItem types
checklist.description: NavLevel has a nullable string parentId, a title string, and an items array. NavItem is a discriminated union with kind: 'notebook' | 'note' and a typed data object.

checklist.name: Core state refs
checklist.description: stack is a ref<NavLevel[]> initialized to [], selectedNoteId is a ref<string | null> initialized to null, and loading is a boolean ref.

checklist.name: leftPanel computed
checklist.description: leftPanel returns stack[length-2] when depth > 1, or stack[0] when depth is 1, or null when the stack is empty.

checklist.name: rightPanel computed
checklist.description: rightPanel returns the last stack entry only when depth > 1 (i.e. it is null at root depth).

checklist.name: openNotebook vs openNotebookFromLeft
checklist.description: openNotebook pushes a new level onto the stack (appends), while openNotebookFromLeft replaces the last entry ([...stack.slice(0,-1), newLevel]). Both clear selectedNoteId.

checklist.name: goBack action
checklist.description: goBack slices the stack to remove the last entry (only when length > 1) and resets selectedNoteId to null.

checklist.name: selectNoteFromRoot
checklist.description: selectNoteFromRoot collapses stack to its first element (stack.slice(0,1)) before setting selectedNoteId, ensuring navigation returns to root depth.
